title: A Systematic View on AI-Based Code Generation
content: In this review, we consider and combine the most recent results from different fields of computer science and software engineering, related to automated code generation using  AI-based tools. First, we provide an historical retrospective in order to establish similarity between industrial revolution and our days. This approach allows adaptation of the historical experience to our days challenges. Next, we provide some results from classical descriptive complexity theory relevant to the scope of our review. In addition, we consider two approaches from Artificial Intelligence (AI): Large Language Model (LLM) and Graph Neural Network (GNN); and the recent results, which provide severe limitations on computability and complexity of both of them. Then, we emphasize the crucial role of automated translations from natural languages to formal languages, used in the previously mentioned results. For our best knowledge, such translations do not exist as for now. However, we show a list of results from different branches of science, which provide some evidence that they should be doable. Moreover, we point out the importance of Test Driven Design (TDD) in automated code generation using AI-based tools. Code maintenance is not less important than code generation from scratch. That is why, any change, made in code must be as local, as possible. The last fact requires precise definition of distances between versions of the desired code at each TDD cycle. Finally, we define a complete workflow, which combines all the features: results from descriptive theory, translation from natural languages to formal languages, code distances as well as combination of TDD, LLM and GNN altogether, that is new. The contribution is dedicated to software engineers and programmers with limited knowledge in computer science and especially in descriptive complexity theory as well as computer science experts with limited experience in practical code writing.
